rows.requirement: fulfillment_method.destinations[] lists addresses (shipping) or retail locations (pickup); selected_destination_id references the chosen one
rows.notes: Lineage: REWORDED. Old description (fulfillment_method.json 2026-04-08): 'Available destinations. For shipping: addresses. For pickup: retail locations.' New description: 'Available destinations for this method. In Business responses, each destination carries a `type` and `id`.' The old two-case (shipping=addresses / pickup=retail locations) phrasing was replaced by a generic self-describing-response statement, because 2026-08-25 adds an entire new '## Destinations' section (fulfillment.md L220-384) generalizing destination typing to any method (well-known `shipping_address`/`business_location` plus negotiated-extension values), superseding the old shipping/pickup-only framing. Also: the old 'Retail Location' concept/schema was renamed 'Business Location Destination' / location_destination.json (see FUL-005 vs old '#### Retail Location' heading, now '#### Business Location Destination'). official_oracle carried forward as true per prior fulfillment_test.py coverage of destination injection/selection; not re-verified against 2026-08-25 conformance suite in this pass. Flagged for review.

rows.requirement: A fulfillment_option MUST include id, title, and totals
rows.quote: "required": ["id", "title"],
rows.notes: Lineage: RENAMED/restructured. In 2026-04-08, fulfillment_option.json alone required ["id","title","totals"]. In 2026-08-25, fulfillment_option.json was decomposed: a NEW shared file fulfillment_option_base.json (title 'Fulfillment Option Base') now requires ["id","title"] (quoted here, L7), and fulfillment_option.json composes it via 'allOf' with a second branch requiring ["totals"] (fulfillment_option.json L13: "required": ["totals"]). The effective combined requirement (id, title, totals all required on a checkout fulfillment_option) is IDENTICAL to 2026-04-08 — only the schema's file/composition structure changed (fulfillment_option_base.json is also reused directly by the new Catalog Discovery 'options[]' shape, per fulfillment.md L580-582). Cites the base file as the more novel change; see FUL-017 for the sibling 'totals' requirement's own prose-level rename.

rows.requirement: options[].totals is the required cost breakdown (an array of `total` objects), replacing the old prose name `total` (a nullable scalar)
rows.quote: | `groups[].options[]`  | `totals`      | Yes      | Cost breakdown: an array of `total` objects             |
rows.notes: Lineage: RENAMED (resolves the divergence the 2026-04-08 row itself flagged). Old Rendering-table row: '| `groups[].options[]`  | `total`       | Yes      | Price in minor units (may be null if not yet available) |' -- the prose named a singular, nullable scalar field `total` even though the schema's actual field was always the array `totals`. New row: '| `groups[].options[]`  | `totals`      | Yes      | Cost breakdown: an array of `total` objects             |' -- prose now uses the correct plural field name `totals` (an array of `total` objects) matching fulfillment_option.json's actual required 'totals' field, and drops the 'may be null if not yet available' nullability language entirely. This is a genuine identifier rename (total -> totals) plus a description rewrite; it converges prose and schema that previously diverged.

rows.requirement: Platforms SHOULD preserve the business-provided option order by default, but MAY re-order options (e.g. to match buyer preferences or surface ranking); platforms MUST preserve the method/option grouping regardless of reordering
rows.notes: Lineage: REWORDED (material change, weakens the old rule). Old text: 'Platforms **SHOULD** render options in the provided order.' New text explicitly permits reordering: 'Platforms **SHOULD** preserve that order, but **MAY** re-order it (e.g. to match known buyer preferences or surface-specific ranking); they **MUST** preserve the method/option grouping.' The old row was a plain SHOULD-preserve-order rule; the new text keeps a SHOULD-preserve-default but adds an explicit MAY-reorder carve-out plus a new MUST about preserving grouping. Flagged for review.

rows.requirement: Platforms SHOULD treat fulfillment as a generic, renderable structure: render each option using title/description/total; present all methods returned; preserve the method/option structure without merging or de-duplicating (the platform, not the business's provided order, now chooses ordering); use available_methods[].description to surface alternatives
rows.quote:
Platforms **SHOULD** treat fulfillment as a generic, renderable structure: ... Preserve the method and option structure—do not merge or de-duplicate;
    the platform chooses ordering
rows.notes: Lineage: REWORDED (one sub-bullet reversed). Old Platform Responsibilities bullets (fulfillment.md 2026-04-08 L203-207) included 'Present options in the order provided by the business' as a sub-requirement of the generic-renderable-structure SHOULD. In 2026-08-25 that bullet is REMOVED and replaced with 'Preserve the method and option structure—do not merge or de-duplicate; the platform chooses ordering' -- i.e. ordering authority flips from the business (provided order) to the platform (chooses ordering), consistent with the new FUL-021 MAY-reorder carve-out. The intro sentence and the 'present all methods returned' / 'use available_methods[].description' bullets are unchanged. Flagged for review.

rows.requirement: A shipping_destination MUST include id and type (type is a required const discriminator "shipping_address"); it is a postal_address plus required id and type
rows.quote:
"required": [
        "id",
        "type"
      ]
rows.notes: Lineage: REWORDED/expanded. Old shipping_destination.json (2026-04-08) required only ["id"] and had no `type` field at all. New shipping_destination.json (2026-08-25) requires ["id", "type"] and adds a `type` property (`"const": "shipping_address"`, description 'Destination type discriminator.'). This is the schema-level counterpart of the new '## Destinations' section's self-describing-response rule (fulfillment.md: 'in Business responses, every destination carries a required `type`'). The old row's parenthetical ('it is a postal_address plus a required id') is no longer complete: it is now a postal_address plus required id AND type. Flagged for review as a substantive addition, not just a rename.

rows.requirement: When the Business accepts a non-null selected_destination_id, its response MUST carry that same selected_destination_id value on the method, and MUST include exactly one destination in that same method's destinations[] whose id equals it, typed as specified in Destinations.
rows.quote:
When the Business accepts a non-null `selected_destination_id`, its response:

* **MUST** carry that same `selected_destination_id` value on the method; and
* **MUST** include exactly one destination in that same method's
    `destinations[]` whose `id` equals it, typed as specified in
    [Destinations](#destinations) — so the response is self-describing whatever
    the ID's source.
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b wave 2): part of the new 'Selection and Location Identity' section (no 04-08 antecedent). Two MUSTs of one integrated echo-back contract registered as a single row since they describe the same response, read as one rule.

rows.requirement: The Business MUST revalidate the selected destination's current availability and terms; recognizing an ID neither reserves inventory nor guarantees eligibility.

availability and terms; recognizing an ID neither reserves inventory nor
guarantees eligibility.
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b wave 2): same new Selection and Location Identity section. Revalidation is an internal business-logic obligation not directly observable from a single request/response pair without a controlled fixture that changes availability between selection and Checkout, hence manual.

rows.requirement: The Business MUST NOT silently substitute another destination: it MUST NOT return a different selected_destination_id, and MUST NOT keep the submitted ID while returning a destination that describes another location.

guarantees eligibility. The Business **MUST NOT** silently substitute another

describes another location. A Business that cannot honor the submitted
selection rejects it rather than replacing it.
rows.notes: NEW at v2026-08-25 (P2b wave 2): the anti-substitution guarantee immediately following FUL-037 in the same section. Three MUST NOT clauses of one integrated no-silent-substitution rule registered as a single row; the three all restate the same 'echo back exactly what was submitted' guarantee from different angles rather than being independently distinguishable obligations.
